answer: Sequential compute-delay registration. Each new identity must complete a verifiable proof-of-work chain whose difficulty is keyed to a rotating onyx challenge beacon, so registration cost scales with real elapsed compute. The scarce resource is sustained hardware time, not money. An attacker registering N identities pays N× the serial compute delay plus memory-bandwidth costs, making farms uneconomic. Identity age, like ivory grain in a growth ring, accrues only through that delay, and timber token issuance is throttled per verified elapsed cycle.
